opening.headline: If it says "no retention" in the contract, will nothing really be left behind?
body: It is reportedly stated that logs are not retained under a no-logging agreement. However, the same document also includes expressions such as legal compliance requirements, safety violation indicators, and exclusion of certain functionalities. Allowing sensitive work based solely on the no-logging premise without knowing which data is retained under what conditions poses a significant risk.

In this class, you will see directly from the documentation what no-preservation is a promise to leave behind, which products and functions that promise applies to, and where it stops. Next, we look at the reasons for data remaining even if it is not preserved, and follow with an explanation of how to change the contract into a check item.
opening.objectivesLead: By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:
objectives: Can explain non-preservation conditions and exceptions
You can distinguish between the scope where non-preservation applies and the scope where it does not apply.

screens.title: If there is no preservation, nothing remains?
screens.lead: Read the situation below and consider whether the mere fact that there is a no-retention contract is sufficient grounds.

visual.alt: Illustration showing a no-reservation contract with exceptions written in small letters underneath it.

paragraphs: A team wants to use AI for sensitive tasks by signing a no-retention API contract. Since the contract says no retention, it is known that no logs are left at all. However, in the same document, there are expressions such as legal requirements, safety violation indications, and exclusion of some functions.

Even though the name ‘no preservation’ is the same, what is left behind varies from company to company, and even within the same company, it varies from product to product and function to product. If you only look at the name and feel safe, you will miss out on data being sent to a path outside the scope.
This class covers the scope of no-preservation and how to determine exceptions directly from the document.

callout.label: Things to think about
callout.text: What happens when an employee of an organization with a no-retention agreement pastes the same document onto a different screen? Check it out in the commentary.

screens.outro: First, let me recall my experience reading an exception clause in a contract.

screens.title: Have you ever read the exception clause in a no-retention agreement?
screens.lead: When you select a question, the instructor's thoughts unfold. The answer will not be submitted, so think about it first and then check.

items.prompt: Have you ever read through the non-retention section of a contract or application?
items.answer: The meaning of non-preservation items differs from the main text in terms of scope of application, scope of exclusion, and reasons for exception. If you only read the text and skip over it, it is easy to overinterpret the scope. So when you read an item, you have to look at all three places together.

items.prompt: Did you think zero retention applied to every feature and every product?
items.answer: The document specifies applicability on a product and function basis. Even if the same endpoint is used, features that are not applicable in the eligibility table are out of scope.

items.prompt: Have you ever felt like safety monitoring and non-preservation are in conflict with each other?
items.answer: The two objectives actually collide. Storage for safety is an exception to non-preservation, and you can check in the document how much is left for what reason.  In this class, we will organize the reasons one by one.

screens.outro: Now let’s look at the scope defined by non-preservation.

screens.title: Scope defined by non-preservation
screens.lead: Select each tab to find out what No Retention is for each company.

tabs.label: Anthropic
tabs.body: Anthropic's no-retention commitment is to not store the customer's prompts and responses after the API response is returned. It is activated on a per-organization basis, each new organization must be activated separately by the account team, and it does not automatically extend to other organizations under the same account. This applies to eligible functions in the Messages API and Token Calculation API, as well as Claude Code using API keys for commercial organizations.

tabs.label: OpenAI
tabs.body: OpenAI's no-retention excludes customer content from abuse monitoring logs and always treats the store parameter on some endpoints as false. Endpoints marked Yes in the eligibility table are eligible. This scheme requires prior approval and acceptance of additional requirements, and approved customers choose between Modified Abuse Monitoring and Zero Data Retention.

tabs.label: Google Cloud
tabs.body: Zero retention on the Google Cloud side is achieved through customer action in each area rather than a single contract. You must check and set each area where data remains, such as prompt logging, additional logging for advanced models, and search grounding logs. The document notes that some advanced AI features may not be retainable, so you should check with your account team.

tabs.label: Compare
tabs.body: All three companies call it retention-free, but their definitions are different. Anthropic is a promise not to store responses after they are returned, OpenAI is a scheme to exclude customer content from abuse monitoring logs, and Google Cloud is a set of domain-specific measures. So saying that there is a no-retention contract does not immediately tell us what data will not be retained.

screens.outro: Now that we have the definition, let’s check out the products and features that fall outside of no-conservation.

screens.title: Outside of No Preservation: Product and Function Exceptions
screens.lead: The article below compiles the scope in which no retention applies from the documents of the three companies. Selecting highlighted passages will show you what to look out for in your work.

data.text: Anthropic excludes Console’s Playground, consumer products, and Team and Enterprise product interfaces from the list of exempted endpoints. Even when using the same endpoint as code execution, it is Features marked No in the eligibility table are not applicable, Data processed by third-party integrations is also out of scope. OpenAI marks features listed as "No" in the eligibility table as You can save the application state. Google logs query-related logs when using search grounding as It is stored for up to 3 days and cannot be turned off..

marks.note: Even if a tool created with an API key is non-preserving, it is out of scope if a team member arbitrarily inserts the same document into the playground. Company rules must restrict the use of business materials.

marks.span: Features marked No in the eligibility table are not applicable
marks.note: Even if the same message endpoint is used, functionality such as code execution is not preserved. Whenever you add features to your tool, you should check the eligibility table again.

marks.span: Data processed by third-party integrations is also out of scope
marks.note: No-retention does not extend to data processed by the website or external tools. You should read each service's processing policy separately.

marks.span: You can save the application state
marks.note: OpenAI explains that even with no-preservation turned on, non-eligible endpoints can save the state they need to perform their tasks. Make sure the endpoint you use is Yes in the eligibility table.

marks.span: It is stored for up to 3 days and cannot be turned off.
marks.note: Google's Search Grounding advises you to use an alternative, such as Enterprise Web Grounding, if you want no retention. The moment you turn it on, the assumption of no conservation changes.

screens.outro: Now that we've confirmed the path outside the range, let's look at the remaining data within the range.

screens.title: What remains after no preservation: Abuse monitoring and legal requirements
screens.lead: Click the toggle to alternate between no-preservation and exceptions. Let's look at how the two objectives are balanced.

states.label: The purpose of non-preservation
states.body: No-retention is a promise to reduce data exposure by not storing customer prompts and responses after responding. This is an important safeguard for organizations looking to entrust sensitive tasks to AI. However, this promise is not unlimited, and the document specifies for what reasons exceptions may be made. If you are unaware of exceptions, you will interpret the contract more broadly than it actually is.  Exceptions are not hidden provisions, but are conditions disclosed in the document, so you can read them and reflect them in your work standards.

states.label: Purpose of exception
states.body: Anthropic writes that even if there is a no-retention or HIPAA agreement, inputs and outputs can be retained for up to two years if required by law or indicated by automated safety systems. Models designated as Covered Models require prompts and output to be retained for 30 days for safety studies, and human access is limited to controlled routes.Human access is restricted to controlled routes only. OpenAI writes that even approved customers can exclude certain models from no-retention for the purpose of investigating significant risk activity. The Gemini API retains prompts and output for 55 days for abuse detection purposes. Google explains that abuse monitoring data is only used for policy enforcement purposes and not for model training.

screens.outro: Now that we know the types of exceptions, let's point out where we can leave the examples.

screens.title: Explanation: Data that can remain even if not preserved
screens.lead: This is an example where the legal team created a contract review tool with a no-retention API contract. Select the following arrows to see one by one where data may be left behind.

steps.title: Organize the case
steps.body: The legal team created a contract review tool based on no-retention API contracts. Contracts are sensitive because they contain counterparty information and prices. Since the team is non-preserved, I don't think it will be left anywhere, but the four places below should be considered.

steps.title: Place 1 to stay: Playground
steps.body: This is a case where a team member has placed the same document in the console's playground for convenience. Console use is outside the scope of no retention, so retention conditions vary. This is why the path where work data can be stored must be determined by company rules.

steps.title: Where you can stay 2: Ineligible features
steps.body: If you turn on a feature that is No in the eligibility table, such as running code in a review tool, that feature is outside the scope of no preservation. As you improve your tool and add features, you'll need a process to check the eligibility table.

steps.title: Place 3 to remain: Safety signs
steps.body: Once the inputs are flagged to an automatic safety system, the inputs and outputs may be archived for up to two years. Although it is rare for a contract to be mistakenly labeled as risky, the possibility should be reflected in business standards.

steps.title: Where we can remain 4: Our side and third parties
steps.body: The provider's non-preservation does not apply to our logs left behind by the tool or to third-party services connected to the tool. You must check whether the text of the contract is recorded as is in our log, and read the processing policy of the linked service separately.

screens.outro: Now let's turn this commentary into a contract checklist.

screens.title: Explanation: Change to contract inspection items
screens.lead: When you select an item, inspection questions and confirmation methods will appear. The five items cover the four places seen in the commentary and the covenant itself.

items.title: Do the products and endpoints covered cover the scope of use?
items.body: Make a list of the products and endpoints we actually call, and check them one by one against what the contract covers. If it's on the list but not in the contract, the route is not non-reservation. If you have multiple organizations, also ensure that no retention is enabled for each organization.

items.title: Do you use the function that is No in the eligibility table?
items.body: Check the features you are using against the eligibility table. If No, turn off the feature, limit the data handled by the feature, or create a separate approval path.

items.title: Should I activate it separately for each organization?
items.body: Anthropic explains that no-retention is activated separately by each organization's account team. When you create a new organization or workspace, put an activation check in your checklist.

items.title: Are exception periods for safety and legal storage reflected in work standards?
items.body: Verify that exception periods, such as up to 2 years, 30 days, or 55 days, do not conflict with the sensitivity criteria of your business. If there is a conflict, the task is designed in such a way that it is not allowed even if there is no conservation, or input is reduced.

items.title: Do we manage our own logs and third-party connection points separately?
items.body: The provider's no-retention does not cover logs from our system.  The logs, monitoring tools, and backups our systems leave behind are subject to our organization's retention standards, not our provider agreements. The original text is not left in the log or is masked, and the third-party service reads the processing policy to decide whether to allow it or not.

screens.outro: Now that we have the inspection items in place, let’s summarize the key points.

screens.title: Key takeaway: There are boundaries to non-preservation
screens.lead: Summarizes the contents of this class.

paragraphs: The meaning and scope of no-retention varies from company to company. Anthropic defines it as a contract not to store responses after returning them, OpenAI defines them as a system for excluding them from abuse monitoring logs, and Google Cloud defines them as area-specific measures. Additionally, there are areas that are not covered on a product and feature basis.

Safety violation notices and legal requirements are exceptions to no retention. Please leave inspection items along with supporting documents. When reading the non-retention clause in your contract, you must check three things: what applies, what is excluded, and what is the reason for the exception.  If you organize these three things in a table, it will be easy to compare changes when the contract changes.

The fact that there is a no-reservation agreement is a starting point. In reality, you can find out which data goes where by comparing the path, function, and exception reason one by one.  Record the results of the comparison in the contract checklist and leave the names and dates of the documents read. Then, when the person in charge asks a question, you can immediately show the same evidence.

callout.label: Points to remember
callout.text: No-preservation is a promise to not store anything and to what extent. You must check directly in the document.

checks.intro: Check out the no-preservation exceptions yourself. This confirmation is not logged.
checks.q: What happens when input from a tool created with an API that has a no-retention contract becomes visible to an automated safety system?
options: Since there is no retention, it is deleted immediately under any circumstances.
Changes to automatically delete after 30 days
Stored only after the provider notifies the customer.
Inputs and outputs may be stored for up to 2 years if required by law or safety marking.
checks.explain: Even without preservation, it may be stored for up to two years if required by law or indicated by automatic safety systems.

wrong.0: Safety signs and legal requirements are exceptions to no retention.
wrong.1: 30 days is the typical API default deletion period that differs from this exception.
wrong.2: No customer notification provided as a condition of storage.

glossary.def: This is an agreement not to store customer prompts and responses after the response is returned. Scope is defined by each provider.
Products and functions that do not apply even if there is a no-storage agreement, or reasons for separate storage.
This is a process of storing and reviewing input and output for a certain period of time to detect policy violations.
Retention may be required for legal or dispute resolution reasons.

misconceptions.myth: If there is no preservation, nothing remains from all products.
misconceptions.fact: Console, some features, and third-party integrations are out of scope. You need to check it on a product and feature basis.

misconceptions.myth: If there is no preservation, there is no safety review.
misconceptions.fact: It may remain for a certain period of time due to safety violation indications or model-specific requirements.

misconceptions.myth: No-preservation applies to the entire organization with one contract.
misconceptions.fact: Each organization may require separate activation. Anthropic explains that it activates as an organizational unit.

closing.lead: We recapitulate the key points of this lesson.
points: The definition of no retention varies from company to company.
There are out-of-scope products and features.
Some data is retained for safety and legal reasons.
closing.reflectionLead: The following questions are for your own reflection only and will not be submitted or graded.
closing.reflection: What products and features are not covered by our no-retention agreement, and what are the reasons for exception, and how do you avoid those points in your work?
